subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 27-year-old man with a known storage disorder is evaluated for worsening fatigue and abdominal fullness. He has massive splenomegaly with a craniocaudal diameter of 22 cm, hemoglobin of 8.8 g/dL, and a platelet count of 71,000/µL. He has had two painful bone crises in the past year and has no neurologic symptoms. He asks about a treatment that specifically replaces the enzyme he is missing.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment for his underlying disease?

options.text: Plasmapheresis with a phytanic acid-restricted diet

explanation_correct: This is Gaucher disease type 1, the non-neuronopathic form, in which glucocerebroside accumulates in macrophages because glucocerebrosidase is deficient. Enzyme replacement with recombinant glucocerebrosidase reduces hepatosplenomegaly, improves anemia and thrombocytopenia, and decreases bone pain. Substrate reduction therapy is an alternative, and enzyme replacement does not reverse preexisting neurologic deficits because glucocerebrosidase does not cross the blood-brain barrier.

explanation_incorrect.B: Recombinant α-galactosidase A is used for Fabry disease, which presents with angiokeratomas, acroparesthesias, and renal failure rather than splenomegaly and bone crises.
explanation_incorrect.C: Idursulfase replaces iduronate-2-sulfatase in Hunter syndrome, a mucopolysaccharidosis with coarse facial features and airway disease.
explanation_incorrect.D: There is no dietary therapy that reduces sphingomyelin storage, and this patient does not have Niemann-Pick disease.
explanation_incorrect.E: Plasmapheresis and a low-phytanic-acid diet are treatments for Refsum disease, a peroxisomal disorder.

educationalObjective: Gaucher disease type 1 is treated with enzyme replacement using recombinant glucocerebrosidase, which improves hematologic and skeletal manifestations.
